statements.subject: server
statements.description: In either case, once the server has issued a success response at the end of the mail data, a formal handoff of responsibility for the message occurs: the protocol requires that a server MUST accept responsibility for either delivering the message or properly reporting the failure to do so (see Sections 6.1, 6.2, and 7.8, below).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Conversely, keyword values presented in the EHLO response that do not begin with "X" MUST correspond to a Standard, Standards-Track, or IESG-approved Experimental SMTP service extension registered with IANA.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If this strategy is employed, the timeout to fall back to an unextended format (if one is available) SHOULD be less than the normal timeout for bouncing as undeliverable.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In particular, if an extension implies that the delivery path normally supports special features of that extension, and an intermediate SMTP system finds a next hop that does not support the required extension, it MAY choose, based on the specific extension and circumstances, to requeue the message and try later and/or try an alternate MX host.

statements.subject: timer

Step 2: relay then opens new connection to xyz.com and forwards the message — illustrating that each relay hop is a distinct SMTP session
statements.trigger: relay connection established to next-hop server
actions: open new SMTP session to next-hop
forward message with updated Received header

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: SMTP systems SHOULD NOT use it unless the server can authenticate the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers MUST continue to accept source route syntax as specified in the main body of this document and in RFC 1123.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: They MAY, if necessary, ignore the routes and utilize only the target domain in the address.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If they do utilize the source route, the message MUST be sent to the first domain shown in the address.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In particular, a server MUST NOT guess at shortcuts within the source route.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD NOT utilize explicit source routing except under unusual circumstances, such as debugging or potentially relaying around firewall or mail system configuration errors.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As discussed in Sections 3.1 and 4.1.1, EHLO SHOULD be used rather than HELO when the server will accept the former.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST continue to accept and process HELO in order to support older clients.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If they are implemented by servers, the implementation model specified in RFC 821 MUST be used and the command names MUST be published in the response to the EHLO command.
